gaps.sentence: The kids spent ___ afternoon playing in the garden.
gaps.explanation: 'The afternoon' and 'the garden' (our garden) are definite in context.

gaps.sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious issue worldwide.
It was ___ best meal I've ever had.
My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich variety of birds lives in the Danube delta.
gaps.explanation: A rich variety of… — variety is countable here, first mention.

gaps.sentence: They sailed across ___ Mediterranean last summer.
gaps.explanation: Seas and oceans take 'the': the Mediterranean.

gaps.sentence: He gave me ___ useful advice about the paperwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — never 'an advice'. Use 'a piece of advice' for one item.
